title: Pal's permanent conjecture: proof for block uniform matrices
summary: Consider a symmetric function $\mathcal{C}(x,y)$ on $[0,1]\times[0,1]$ which is twice continuously differentiable up to the boundary, and which satisfies $ \mathcal{C}(x,y)=\mathcal{C}(1-x,1-y)$. Let $A^{(n)} = \big(a^{(n)}_{i,j}\, :\, i,j \in [n]\big)$ be the matrix with entries $a^{(n)}_{i,j}\, =\, \exp(-\mathcal{C}(i/n,j/n))$. Soumik Pal conjectured the asymptotics $$\operatorname{perm}\big(A^{(n)}\big)/n!\sim \exp\big(n Λ[\mathcal{C}]\big)/ \sqrt{\mathcal{D}[\mathcal{C}]}$$ as $n \to \infty$ for known functionals that arise naturally in the context of entropy regularized optimal…
